tasks.title: Orbit the view
tasks.hint: Hold the orbit button and drag. With nothing selected the camera turns around the middle of the view.

tasks.title: Slide the camera sideways
tasks.hint: Pan keeps the point under the cursor anchored, so the scene tracks your hand instead of drifting.

tasks.title: Add a floor
tasks.hint: Press {key:Blendon/Context Menu} on an empty spot, open Add, then pick Plane. It lands where you clicked, and everything after this stands on it.

tasks.title: Zoom toward a corner of the floor
tasks.hint: Point at a corner of the plane and scroll - you close in on that corner, not on the middle of the view.

tasks.title: Drop a cube onto the floor
tasks.hint: Point at the floor, hold the key, flick toward Cube and let go. Direction is all that counts, and the cube lands on the floor under the cursor.

tasks.title: Frame the cube
tasks.hint: The new cube is selected, so this fills the view with it. Press again to step through bounds, pivot and close.

tasks.title: Orbit around the cube
tasks.hint: The same orbit, now with the cube selected: the camera turns around the cube instead of the view's own pivot.

chapters.title: Grab and Move
chapters.subtitle: One key, no handle to hit

tasks.title: Grab the cube and drop it
tasks.hint: Press the key and the cube follows the cursor across the screen. A left click or Enter drops it there.

tasks.title: Change your mind
tasks.hint: Grab again, then right-click or press Esc: the cube jumps back exactly where it was, with nothing left in the undo history.

tasks.title: Slide along one axis
tasks.hint: Grab, then press X: the cube can only travel along X now. Y or Z switch the axis, and a click drops it.

tasks.title: Lift it exactly two metres
tasks.hint: Grab, press Y for up, type 2 and press Enter. The mouse stops driving the moment the first digit lands.

tasks.title: Drop it back onto the floor
tasks.hint: The cube is floating now. This rests its bounds on whatever is below it, here the floor.

tasks.title: Slide it across the floor
tasks.hint: Grab, then hold the plane lock key and press Y: the cube moves along X and Z but never leaves the floor.

tasks.title: Move it in grid steps
tasks.hint: Grab and hold the snap key while you move: the cube lands on Unity's snap increments, ticks show the steps.

tasks.title: Fine-tune its position
tasks.hint: Grab and hold the precision key: the cube moves a fraction of the distance the cursor does.

chapters.title: Rotate and Scale
chapters.subtitle: The same gesture, two more ways

tasks.title: Turn the cube
tasks.hint: The rotate key works like the grab: the angle follows the cursor around the pivot, a click keeps it.

tasks.title: Turn it exactly 45 degrees
tasks.hint: Rotate, press Y to turn around the up axis, type 45 and press Enter.

tasks.title: Slide along the cube's own axis
tasks.hint: Grab and press X twice: the second press switches to the cube's own X, which now runs at 45 degrees.

tasks.title: Scale it up
tasks.hint: Move away from the pivot to grow, toward it to shrink, and click to keep the size.

tasks.title: Put the size back
tasks.hint: Hold the Reset menu's key and flick to Scale. Only the size goes back, the turn and the position stay.

tasks.title: Add a second cube
tasks.hint: Add another one the same way, from the context menu's Add, or duplicate the first with {key:Main Menu/Edit/Duplicate}. Leave a gap between the two.

tasks.title: Snap a corner onto a corner
tasks.hint: Grab the new cube, then hold the vertex key near one of its corners. Move it onto a corner of the first cube and click while still holding.

tasks.title: Stand it on top of the other
tasks.hint: Grab and hold the aim key over the first cube: the selection follows the surface under the cursor. Click on its top face.

chapters.title: Tools and Handles
chapters.subtitle: When you want a handle after all

tasks.title: Pick the Move tool
tasks.hint: Hold the key and flick to Move. Unity's own tool keys and toolbar work too, the menu just keeps them under one key.

tasks.title: Drag an arrow
tasks.hint: The arrows work as they always did. They just draw Blender's way and take every key from the last chapters.

tasks.title: Drag a plane square
tasks.hint: The small square between two arrows moves along both of those axes at once.

tasks.title: Line the arrows up with the cube
tasks.hint: Hold the Orientation menu's key and flick to Local: the arrows follow the cube's own 45 degree turn.

tasks.title: Switch to the Rotate tool
tasks.hint: Flick to Rotate in the Tools menu, or use Unity's own key. The next three tasks need its rings.

tasks.title: Turn a rotation ring
tasks.hint: Drag one of the coloured rings, the angle follows the cursor around the pivot.

tasks.title: Aim the cube at the other one
tasks.hint: Drag a ring and hold the aim key: the cube turns to face whatever is under the cursor. Point at the other cube and let go.

tasks.title: Turn the cube around its corner
tasks.hint: Press the key, click a corner to settle the gizmo on it, then drag a ring: the cube swings around that corner.

tasks.title: Keep that corner as a pivot
tasks.hint: Still on the corner, press Enter: an empty takes its place with the cube under it, so the cube now turns around it for good.

tasks.title: Box-select both cubes
tasks.hint: Drag from an empty spot across both cubes. Everything the box touches is picked, it doesn't have to fit inside.

tasks.title: Add to the box, or take away
tasks.hint: Drag with {key:Scene View/Add Box Select} to add what the box touches, or with {key:Scene View/Invert Box Select} to take it away.

tasks.title: Group the two cubes
tasks.hint: With both selected, press {key:Blendon/Context Menu} and pick Group: an empty is made with both cubes under it.

tasks.title: Step up to the parent
tasks.hint: Select a cube in the group, or the one under the pivot you kept, then step up: what holds it is selected instead.
tasks.needs: Select a cube under the group or the pivot first

tasks.title: Step down to the children
tasks.hint: From that parent, step down: the cubes under it are selected again.
tasks.needs: Select the group or the pivot first

tasks.title: Click a selected cube again
tasks.hint: Select a cube under the parent, then click it once more: the selection moves up to what holds it, like stepping up.
tasks.needs: Select a cube under the group or the pivot first

tasks.title: Step back through selections
tasks.hint: Browser-style back and forward for what you had selected: {key:Blendon/History/Undo Selection} goes back, {key:Blendon/History/Redo Selection} goes forward.

tasks.title: Turn both cubes in place
tasks.hint: With both selected, flick to Individual Origins in the Pivot Point menu, then rotate: each cube spins around its own centre.

tasks.title: Match one cube's turn to the other
tasks.hint: Select both, the last one clicked is the active one. Press {key:Blendon/Context Menu}, then Align to Active, Rotation: the other takes its turn.

tasks.title: Look from the front, the side and the top
tasks.hint: The axis views: front on {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/View Front}, right on {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/View Right} and top on {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/View Top}. Back, left and bottom look from the opposite side, on {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/View Back}, {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/View Left} and {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/View Bottom}. NumLock has to be on for the keypad.

tasks.title: Switch between perspective and flat
tasks.hint: Toggles the view between perspective and orthographic, handy right after an axis view.

tasks.title: Orbit in steps
tasks.hint: Each press turns the view by a fixed step around the pivot: {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/Orbit Left} left, {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/Orbit Right} right, {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/Orbit Up} up, {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/Orbit Down} down.

tasks.title: Lock onto an axis while orbiting
tasks.hint: Start the orbit drag first, then hold this key: near a world axis the view locks onto it and goes flat. Let go for a free orbit again.

tasks.title: Roll the view 90°
tasks.hint: Hold the key and flick the mouse in any direction - the view rolls 90° that way and lands squarely on the nearest axis view.

tasks.title: Click an axis on the orientation gizmo
tasks.hint: The ball in the corner of the view: click a handle to swing round to that axis, drag inside it to orbit, middle-click to toggle projection.

tasks.title: Change the view without a numpad
tasks.hint: Hold the View menu's key and flick to Top. The same views and the projection toggle, under one key.

tasks.title: Look through the camera
tasks.hint: Lines the view up with the scene's camera, so you see what the game will see. No camera yet? Add one from the Add menu.

tasks.title: Go back to where you were looking
tasks.hint: Back and forward through camera positions, like selection history but for the view.

tasks.title: Isolate one cube, then leave
tasks.hint: Hides everything else while you work. The same key brings the scene back.

chapters.title: Pie Menus and You
chapters.subtitle: Menus on a key, keys of your own

tasks.title: See the scene as wireframe
tasks.hint: Hold the Draw Mode menu's key and flick to Wireframe.

tasks.title: Latch a pie open and click
tasks.hint: Tap the same key instead of holding it: the menu stays up, and a left click on Shaded brings the scene back.

tasks.title: Flip wireframe on and off
tasks.hint: One key between the current look and wireframe, without opening the menu.

tasks.title: Run a pie item by its number
tasks.hint: Every item is numbered. Hold the Tools menu's key and press 1 to run its first item without aiming.

tasks.title: Keep snapping on for every move
tasks.hint: Flick to Grid in the Snapping menu, then grab the cube: it steps along the grid without holding a key. Flick again to turn it off.

tasks.title: Change a key to one you like
tasks.hint: Every key in this tutorial can be changed. Pick any shortcut on a feature page or the Keyboard page and give it a new key.
